title: Types that bite
summary: The type names, casting, == versus ===, integer division, and float precision.

blocks.html:
PHP names seven types in lowercase: int, float, string, bool, array, null, and object for the instances that chapter 09 builds.

gettype() returns the type as a string, and it uses the long names — integer, double, boolean — while var_dump() says int, float, bool. Same types, two spellings.

Casting converts a value on demand, with (int), (float), (string) or (bool) in front of it. From a string, PHP takes the leading number and ignores everything after it — handy with messy input, dangerous when it silently erases a mistake.

blocks.title: four casts
blocks.code:
<?php

var_dump((int) "42");         // clean number
var_dump((int) "42 apples");  // the rest is dropped
var_dump((int) 3.99);         // truncation, not rounding
var_dump((float) "1.5");
var_dump((string) 12);
var_dump((bool) "0");         // the string is not empty, but it is "0"
var_dump((bool) "");
var_dump((bool) "false");     // any non-empty string except "0" is true
blocks.output:
int(42)
int(42)
int(3)
float(1.5)
string(2) "12"
bool(false)
bool(false)
bool(true)

blocks.html:
Now the operator that causes the most bugs in PHP. == converts the two sides until they can be compared, then compares. === compares value and type with no conversion, so a string is never equal to a number.

Two PHP 8 rules matter: a number compared with a non-numeric string is now compared as a string, so 0 == "abc" is false (in PHP 7 it was true, the classic surprise), while two numeric strings are still compared as numbers.

blocks.title: == against ===
blocks.code:
<?php

var_dump("1" == 1);        // converted, then equal
var_dump("1" === 1);       // different types
var_dump("1" == "01");     // two numeric strings: compared as numbers
var_dump(0 == "abc");      // false since PHP 8
var_dump(1 == "1abc");     // false since PHP 8
var_dump(null == false);   // both loosely empty
blocks.output:
bool(true)
bool(false)
bool(true)
bool(false)
bool(false)
bool(true)

blocks.title: loose and strict comparison
blocks.ascii:
"1" == 1       convert, then compare      true
  "1" === 1      compare value and type     false

  "1" == "01"    both numeric strings       true
  "1" === "01"   different characters       false

  == asks: do these mean the same value?
  === asks: same value, same type, no conversion.

blocks.title: ask before you convert
blocks.code:
<?php

var_dump(is_int(42));
var_dump(is_int("42"));       // a string is not an int
var_dump(is_numeric("42"));   // but it is numeric
var_dump(is_numeric("42abc"));
var_dump(is_numeric(" 42"));  // leading space is still numeric

blocks.title: numeric strings join arithmetic
blocks.code:
<?php

$amount = "1500";

echo $amount + 100, "\n";   // the plus converts the numeric string
echo $amount . 100, "\n";   // the dot concatenates instead
var_dump($amount);          // the variable itself is untouched

blocks.title: integer division, remainder, and float imprecision
blocks.code:
<?php

$minutes = 1530;

echo intdiv($minutes, 60), " hours and ", $minutes % 60, " minutes\n";
echo $minutes / 60, "\n";      // the plain slash returns a float

var_dump(0.1 + 0.2);            // not 0.3
var_dump(0.1 + 0.2 == 0.3);     // and not equal to 0.3 either
var_dump(round(0.1 + 0.2, 2));
blocks.output:
25 hours and 30 minutes
25.5
float(0.30000000000000004)
bool(false)
float(0.3)

blocks.html:
/ always gives a float; intdiv() gives whole units and % gives the remainder. And 0.1 + 0.2 is not 0.3, because binary fractions cannot hold those decimals exactly — never compare two floats with ===, compare their difference against a small tolerance, or round() first.

The same weak conversion can bite in the other direction: "abc" + 5 throws a TypeError in PHP 8. A file that opens with declare(strict_types=1) refuses the quiet conversions for function arguments, so strlen(42) throws instead of reading 42 as text.

blocks.title: declare(strict_types=1) is a file-level promise
blocks.code:
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// Below this line, an argument must already be the declared type.
var_dump(strlen("42"));

// Without the declare, strlen(42) would quietly return int(2).
// With it, that same call throws a TypeError instead.

quiz.why: == converts the string to an integer and compares 1 with 1. === also compares types, and a string is not an integer, so it is false.
gettype() uses the historical C names: integer, double, boolean, string. var_dump() reports the same value as float(4.2).

options: PHP rounds floats when it prints them
Binary fractions cannot store 0.1, 0.2 and 0.3 exactly
=== converts the sum to a string first
quiz.why: The stored sum is 0.30000000000000004, so the strict comparison fails. Compare a difference against a tolerance, or round before comparing.

exercise.brief: Start from $input = "42"; and print exactly four lines with var_dump(): the value cast to int, cast to float, compared strictly against the integer 42, and is_numeric("42 apples").
exercise.hint: A cast goes in front of the expression: var_dump((int) $input); and the strict comparison is $input === 42.
